name: Journeys
title: Journeys: operator and guest paths and what can go wrong

BANDS.s: Select a predefined restaurant journey and understand its trigger.
Choose content, channel and provider prerequisites.
Follow event driven visits, scheduled checks and consent.
Trace eligible recipients into dispatch and guest actions.
Edit, disable and reconcile individual runs.
Planned canvas and return attribution rules from the current PRD.

NODES.d: Open the restaurant's existing stage-based Journeys surface, with categories, channel filters, enablement and results.
e: A category filter hides an enabled reminder
Staff assume no send is active

NODES.d: Choose a New, Occasional, Regular or Lost guest stage. The stage set depends on the restaurant's Regular and Lost durations in Guest Book.
e: Changing segment settings changes which stages are available
Existing reminder no longer matches the intended guests
An impossible duration combination leaves the list empty

NODES.t: Select a date or loyalty trigger
NODES.d: Birthday offers month before, week before and on the day. Anniversary uses week before and on the day. Loyalty lists sign-up, tier and redemption reminders.
e: Operator treats first visit anniversary as birthday
Guest gets the wrong occasion message
An enabled loyalty reminder is assumed to have a populated audience
Operator expects sends that never occur

NODES.d: Open the customer view for the stage and selected channel. Presence of a phone or email alone does not establish permission to send.
e: Audience preview includes a reachable but unsubscribed guest
Operator compares a stage preview with an earlier run

NODES.d: Configure the channel for the stage. Email and text use different content, destination and eligibility rules.
e: Changing channel leaves the old channel's copy displayed
The guest has only the other channel available

NODES.d: Configure the email and its layout or uploaded template. Check subject, layout, links and the personal unsubscribe destination.
e: Template preview contains the correct link but the sent HTML omits it
Stored template image fails to load in the inbox

NODES.d: Select the deal, spotlight or menu item where applicable and verify that it belongs to the restaurant and remains available.
e: Deactivated spotlight is removed but copy still advertises it
A deal expires between selection and delivery

NODES.d: Edit body, optional link and optional media. The body counter changes with the link allowance.
e: Adding a link leaves existing copy outside the allowed length
Operator cannot save the final message
An old media URL remains after a channel change

NODES.d: Saving a text configuration or enabling a text journey checks restaurant verification. The relay also needs the marketing messaging service.
e: Verification changes after save and before dispatch
Setup for a different restaurant appears ready
Operator tries to enable an unusable channel

NODES.d: Save channel, body and referenced content. Deal, item and spotlight selections can be cleared by an edit.
e: Two operators save different versions and overwrite each other
Removing an attachment leaves its old call to action in the body

NODES.d: Switch on the selected stage. The status service can dispatch when a send is requested, the stage is enabled and it has a body.
e: Switch appears on after the service rejects text verification
Operator expects sends from a disabled stage
A request to enable with immediate sending is repeated
Guests may receive the same reminder twice

NODES.d: For an identified guest, the visit handler uses the order count supplied for that event. One selects the first visit and two selects the second visit. Sending also requires an enabled current stage for the restaurant and a guest eligible for its channel.
e: An order event arrives with a visit count of two for a guest completing their first qualifying visit
The guest can receive the second visit message early
The first visit is anonymous when the event is processed and staff identify the guest later
The guest may miss the first visit message unless a qualifying event is processed after attachment

NODES.d: The worker loads current, enabled journeys for the restaurant. The segment evaluator matches the guest's stage before dispatch.
e: A stage is disabled while a previously selected batch is pending
Segment recalculation and the scheduled check run in different orders
Guest enters the wrong reminder stage

NODES.d: Birthday uses the stored birth date. Anniversary derives from the first visit date. Calendar checks include dates crossing into the next year.
e: A December check misses a January birthday
Guest misses the selected advance notice
Leap day or a missing first visit date places the guest in the wrong daily group
Reminder arrives on the wrong date

NODES.d: The recurring worker has a loyalty branch, but its recipient lookup in this checkout returns an empty list. Trace any alternative sender separately.
e: A loyalty sign-up stage shows enabled but produces no scheduled recipients
A zero-recipient result is read as no loyalty activity

NODES.d: Email requires subscription. Text requires an opted-in, valid US phone number. A matching stage must also have usable content. The worker reserves one text credit per selected recipient for SMS or two when the journey includes media.
e: Email permission is used as a substitute for SMS consent
Guest with valid consent is dropped after phone formatting changes

NODES.d: The service reserves monthly usage by restaurant and journey recipient group. A blocked reservation records an error and excludes that group from sending.
e: Campaign usage consumes the remaining allowance before the journey reservation
Retry reserves usage twice for the same group

NODES.d: Eligible recipients are grouped by channel and split into batches of up to 50. Keep the stage, location and content tied to the batch.
e: A failure after the first batch leaves the remainder unsent
Some otherwise eligible guests are missed
Batch is retried after partial success

NODES.d: The relay supports stored HTML and a bulk-template path. It counts send outcomes and supplies guest-specific unsubscribe links.
e: One template fetch fails for a whole batch
Provider accepts a message but AIO cannot match its event
Delivery or open is missing from history

NODES.d: The relay uses the restaurant's marketing text configuration and duplicate handling. It records outcomes by recipient where available. The shared inbound SMS worker records opt outs for future audience selection.
e: Provider accepts a message but later delivery fails
A retry skips a guest whose first attempt never reached the provider

NODES.d: The guest opens the email or text and follows the offer or destination. Receipt, click and a restaurant order are separate events.
e: Saved link opens a different location
Guest cannot redeem the advertised deal
Email opens are interpreted as a completed return visit

NODES.d: The guest can use the email unsubscribe link or withdraw SMS consent. Verify the next journey selection with the updated preference.
e: A queued batch still contains the guest after opt out
Opting out of texts changes an unrelated email preference

NODES.d: History exposes time, channel, total, sent and failed. Inspect customer results and distinguish failed attempts from ineligible guests.
e: Guests excluded before dispatch appear to be a provider failure
Summing retries counts the same guest multiple times

NODES.d: Reopen content and save changes. Check messages already selected separately from subsequent runs.
e: A queued message contains an earlier deal while the preview shows the replacement
A removed offer still appears in uploaded email HTML
Guest is sent to a retired promotion

NODES.d: Disable the stage to exclude it from future recurring selections. Verify already dispatched messages separately before re-enabling.
e: Previously queued messages continue after the operator expects a full stop
Re-enabling repeats a stage already received by the same person

NODES.d: Reconcile eligibility, sent and failed counts, consent and provider delivery for the affected guest and channel.
e: A zero-send run is closed as healthy without inspecting quota or eligibility

NODES.d: The stage summary uses total recipients for sent and successful send attempts for delivered. Compare these labels with run history and actual provider delivery events.
e: A provider-accepted text fails later but is counted as delivered in stage statistics
Recipients selected for an attempt are counted as sent after a partial failure

NODES.d: The PRD defines Bring back new guests and Win back lost guests, initially off, with a restaurant deal attached to each. Enabling starts the defined entry rules.
e: Starter deal is created twice when setup is retried
Inactive restaurant is enabled without the operator's decision

NODES.d: Done stages a single edit. Apply changes publishes the validated canvas after the operator reviews its impact. Revised waits retain their original start.
e: Moving a step sends it twice to the same entry
Changing an entry rule moves guests already in progress

NODES.d: The PRD allows one running journey per guest. A qualifying return can occur during the journey or within 30 days after its last step. Where both journeys reached the guest, the most recent delivered message determines credit.
e: Both journeys take credit for one order
A qualifying return fails to cancel later reminders
Guest receives an offer after meeting the goal

NOTES: The internal Marketing sidebar opens the existing stage list, with editing and history. The Journeys 2.0 canvas remains represented by the upcoming steps.
The existing stage, worker and relay paths are distinct from the Journeys 2.0 canvas. The three upcoming steps are based on the Notion PRD dated 19 November 2026.

The recurring loyalty-stage recipient lookup returns an empty list. Loyalty registration and eligible guest imports can send a separate transactional welcome. Its receipt does not confirm that a recurring stage ran.

Native device event delivery, behaviour of an already queued batch after disabling a stage, production scheduling and carrier receipt require operational checks. No directly matching PROD incident was supplied.
